issue_context.title: Supla integration is exceeding API calls limit.
issue_context.body:
<!-- READ THIS FIRST:
  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/
  - Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/releases
  - Do not report issues for integrations if you are using custom components or integrations.
  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
Supla integration is exceeding API calls limit. After contacting with the supla developers I came to know that they have recently set a limit which is 1000 per hour. My server constantly reports the following error
`Server: svr6.supla.org not configured. API call returned: {'status': 429, 'message': 'You have reached your API rate limit. Slow down.'}` 


## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: Home Assistant 0.109.5
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): unknown
- Operating environment (Home Assistant/Supervised/Docker/venv): Docker (rpi 4)
- Integration causing this issue: Supla
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/supla/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`


```yaml
supla:
  servers:
    - server: svr6.supla.org
      access_token:  "redacted"
```

## Traceback/Error logs


```txt
Server: svr6.supla.org not configured. API call returned: {'status': 429, 'message': 'You have reached your API rate limit. Slow down.'}
```

## Additional information

Hey there @mwegrzynek, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with a integration (`supla`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L382) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

@bonon Can you tell me, how many Supla devices you have? Supla's API doesn't allow querying device states in batches (at least as far as I know) and the integration has to call the API at least once for a device per scan interval (AFAIK 15s?). That gives roughly 240 API calls per device per hour, so max. 4 devices with this API limit.

A super quick solution is to deploy your own Supla Cloud server. It's quite easy, I've done it myself, see [Supla Docker](https://github.com/SUPLA/supla-docker). It works quite well and, as a bonus, your devices won't have to talk with anything outside your home LAN. Longer term solution would be to enable scan interval configuration for Supla devices and sacrifice interactivity in bigger instalations (at least until the Supla guys develop a callback mechanism for reporting device state changes).

5 devices exceed the limit, so calculation seems to be right :) it would be perfect to have supla cloud as hassos addon 🤔 another option may be the https://github.com/pawelka/hassio-addons/tree/master/supla-mqtt-integration
The MQTT integration is also an option: with it you can skip this integration entirely and use HA's MQTT components (sacrificing a bit of simplicity and autoconfiguration).

Unfortunately, it seems it's a bit complicated to make this pull interval configurable. I have to research it a little bit more (and currently I'm very short on time). A local Supla Docker installation is the quickest solution ATM.

Unfortunatelly supla-mqtt-integration is not available for arms, so it's not a way for rpi + hass os. What is more setup of Supla Docker on the same rpi with hass os seems not to be so simple (supla uses docker compose with a few dockers).

AI Speaker project prepare in own integration based on official HA integration this interval as configurable, please see below link, maybe it's will be a chance to add this funcjonality (scan interval) to official HA integration.

https://ai-speaker.discourse.group/t/interacja-ais-supla/424/3

I finally had some time to implement a scan interval setting in Supla integration. You can test it before I try to upstream it  [here](/mwegrzynek/core/tree/supla-interval-config). This patch adds a `scan_interval` variable to server config and lowers integration level `SCAN_INTERVAL` to 10 seconds. An example configuration below:

```yaml
supla:
    servers:
        - server: srv1.supla.com.pl
          access_token: <ACCESS_TOKEN>
          scan_interval: 
            seconds: 150
```
I'll be grateful for feedback!
Wow, great! is there a way to test this with existing HA instance or do I have to setup new one from the branch?

I think it will be best to set up a new instance. A quick & dirty solution is to replace `homeassistant/components/supla/__init__.py` file in your installation with the one from the  `supla-interval-config` branch.
where I find homeassistant/components/supla/__init__.py in my instalation HA i check via samba and i dont see this folder and file?

It depends on how you installed HA in the first place. if you are using a venv, then it will be in its lib/python3.x/site-packages/homeassistant directory. Please look for **`__init__.py`** not **`init.py`**.

As I said before, it will be easier to make a test instance from the branch. Please follow this [guide](https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/installation/virtualenv/), but replace step 4 with:
```
git clone https://github.com/mwegrzynek/core.git
cd core
git checkout supla-interval-config
pip install -e .
```
To all interested: please see the PR mentioned above. It implements  bulk update logic that was in the API all the time (I somehow missed it). Feedback welcome!
